topic: Massage for teachers back in the classroom

slides.headline: Back on your feet all term?
slides.sub: Where remedial massage fits for teachers.

slides.title: Where teachers tend to feel it
slides.body: Standing at the board, bending over low desks, marking at the kitchen table and carrying tubs of books. Calves, lower back, neck and shoulders often feel it in the opening weeks of term.

slides.title: What massage can help with
slides.body: Remedial massage can ease muscle tightness and help you feel less stiff after a long week. It doesn't replace strength or movement, but it can make settling back into routine more comfortable.

slides.title: Pair it with small habits
slides.body: Crouch or sit beside students rather than bending over. Rest one foot on a low step when standing. Mark at a table with the pile raised, not hunched on the couch.

slides.title: Timing your sessions
slides.body: Many teachers find a session early in term and another around the busy middle weeks works well. Booking a time when you can rest afterwards, rather than rushing back, can help too.

slides.title: When massage isn't enough
slides.body: Pain that wakes you, spreads down an arm or leg, comes with numbness or keeps building despite rest is worth a physio or GP assessment rather than more massage.

slides.headline: Ready for a looser term one?
slides.body: Our remedial massage therapists work on the areas teaching loads up, and suggest simple habits to go with it. Book online — link in bio.

caption:
Teachers: a few weeks into term and your calves and back already know it?

Standing at the board, bending over low desks, carrying tubs of books and marking hunched at home all add up. Calves, the lower back, neck and shoulders usually feel it first.

Remedial massage can ease that tightness and help you feel less stiff by Friday. It works well alongside small habits: crouch beside students rather than bending, rest a foot on a low step when standing, and mark at a table instead of the couch.

Pain that wakes you, spreads down a limb or comes with numbness is worth a physio or GP assessment instead.

Our remedial massage therapists at Hybrid Physiotherapy can help you through term one. Book online via the link in bio.
